summary.text: The pelagic zone is the open ocean's water column, the free water away from shore where sea life can swim in any direction.
With depth, pressure rises while light and temperature fall, so the column divides into up to five layers and life thins out the deeper you go.
Nearly all of the ocean's primary production happens in the sunlit top layer, which holds about 90% of marine life, and the whole pelagic ecosystem rests on phytoplankton.

items.prompt: A clam is buried in seafloor mud while a tuna swims far out at sea. Which one lives in the pelagic zone?
items.explain: The pelagic zone is the open water itself; clams living at the very bottom belong to the benthic zone instead.

items.prompt: The sunlit top layer is a thin slice of the open ocean. Roughly what share of marine life is concentrated there?
items.explain: Nearly all primary production happens in the sunlit layer, and about 90% of marine life is concentrated there.

items.prompt: Many animals in the mesopelagic zone, a few hundred meters down, make their own light. Why did that ability evolve there?
items.explain: The mesopelagic zone gets only a trace of sunlight, and many animals there have evolved bioluminescence because of that lack of light.

items.prompt: Some mesopelagic animals swim up into the surface layer at night and sink again by day. What draws them up?

options.label: Feeding in the richer top layer

items.explain: Some mesopelagic creatures rise to the epipelagic zone at night to feed, where nearly all of the ocean's primary production happens.

items.prompt: In the pitch-black bathypelagic zone there is no sunlight for plants. How do most animals there get by?

options.label: Making food from sunlight leaking down
Grazing on seaweed that grows there
Eating debris that drifts down from above

items.explain: Most creatures there live on detritus called marine snow falling from the zones above, or by preying on other animals in the zone.

items.prompt: Far from any coast, a whole open-ocean food web of fish, squid and whales ultimately depends on what?
items.explain: The pelagic ecosystem is based on phytoplankton, and nearly all primary production happens in the sunlit surface layer.
